Review.Independence: I received the revision 3 contract, the complete diff between the named revisions, the cited rules, both run receipts and their check logs, and the status and check reports. I had no part in authoring the change and had not seen the authoring discussion.

Finding.Text: recoveredResult infers ownership from filenames shared by distinct legal check IDs. If trace T has a declared log and the next selected check is T.output, killing during T leaves T.output.log. Recovery assigns that file to both checks and records T.output as interrupted even though it never started. Case-only differences also alias on case-insensitive filesystems. A2 and K1 require each artifact to attest the specific check.

Killing the runner alone releases SQLite ownership while a surviving check process retains its writable stdout and stderr file descriptor. On POSIX the shell is explicitly detached. Recovery hashes and publishes the original file, so later output from the child changes the bytes named by the immutable receipt. This breaks the log-hash guarantee in A2 and K1. Recovery needs a stable artifact for its receipt.

CK1 uses IDs with distinct filenames and kills the process tree before adoption. Both the false attempt in F1 and a changed log hash in F2 pass CK1. Cover colliding legal IDs and kill the runner alone while a surviving check writes again after recovery.

recoverOne checks for the header before checking the lock. While saveHeader is validating or renaming its temporary file, the runner already owns the reservation. Concurrent recovery can therefore report a missing header, exit 1 and suggest fresh execution for a healthy run. The documented busy-reservation diagnostic is live.

Review.Adequacy: The final test log shows the amendment, retained identities, declared-log fallback, absent log, concurrent adoption, close refusal and malformed-header cases passing. The filename-alias and parent-only-kill cases in F3 can both corrupt the recovered evidence while this command passes.
Review.Rule: F1 attributes one log to an unattempted check. F2 allows the receipt's saved hash to disagree with the bytes at its recorded path.
L-36 identifies the observed missing identity, the alternative, the cost and a concrete retirement condition.
